request.prompt:
You are clustering code review findings from the same PR. For each PAIR below, decide whether the two findings describe the SAME underlying issue — same root cause in the same code location. Different wording is fine. A finding about a DIFFERENT defect in the same file or function is NOT the same issue. Severity or aspect differences of the same root cause ARE the same issue.


For THIS scoring pass, duplicate equivalence is stricter than sharing a root cause.
You must compare the COMPLETE MATERIAL CLAIMS, including mechanism, triggering
conditions, execution path, and consequence. The same line or broad concern does
not establish equivalence. A report of wrong-category selection, a case/rename
mismatch, a crash, and a silent fallback are different claims even at one lookup.
An inactive/unbound API concern and an alleged active user-facing failure differ.
A compound report with an additional material claim does NOT equal its subset.
Differences only in wording, severity, or hedging do not create separate claims.
If the claimed mechanisms, triggers or consequences conflict, or one report adds
an unsupported/different material factual claim, return same=false. You are NOT
verifying which claim is true; do not repair or reinterpret either report to make
them match. If unsure whether their full claims are equivalent, return false.

For every numbered pair, extract what A and B actually CLAIM into mechanism,
trigger and consequence. Then list material_differences and give your equivalence
verdict, confidence and reason. same=true requires no material differences.
Return ONLY this JSON object, with EVERY pair index exactly once:
{"pairs":[{"pair":1,"a":{"mechanism":"...","trigger":"...","consequence":"..."},"b":{"mechanism":"...","trigger":"...","consequence":"..."},"material_differences":[],"same":true,"confidence":0.9,"reason":"..."}]}

PAIR 8:
A: lark, msteams (office365video) and webex route refreshes through refreshOAuthTokens but never apply parseRefreshTokenResponse, so the sync endpoint's response is consumed through legacy error handlers with no schema validation and no refresh_token placeholder injection. A sync response missing app-specific fields (e.g. lark's refresh_token/expire, webex's expires_in) is persisted verbatim into credential.key, silently degrading those integrations in sync mode.
B: The sharing-mode response validation (parseRefreshTokenResponse) is applied at only four of the ten refresh sites this PR rewires (google, office365-calendar, zoom, salesforce); msteams, hubspot, lark, webex, zoho-bigin and zohocrm receive sharing-mode responses with no validation at all. In sharing deployments a malformed endpoint response fails loudly for the validated apps but is persisted unvalidated for the other six, so the same parent-app bug produces inconsistent corruption across apps and is far harder to diagnose.

PAIR 9:
A: The literal string "refresh_token" is written into the parsed credential data whenever it lacks refresh_token — which the minimum schema guarantees in sharing mode by stripping the field — and callers persist that placeholder into credential.key with nothing marking it as a sentinel. A self-hoster who enables sharing (Office365's real refresh_token is overwritten by this sentinel on the first sync refresh) and later removes CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT has every affected credential send the literal string "refresh_token" to the provider as its actual refresh token, killing those integrations with an invalid_grant that gives no hint the stored value is a placeholder.
B: When sharing is enabled, `minimumTokenResponseSchema` strips every field except `access_token` (the computed `[z.string().toString()]` keys collapse to a single literal non-matching key), so `data.refresh_token` is always undefined and the code overwrites the credential's real refresh token with the literal string `"refresh_token"`, which callers then persist via `prisma.credential.update`. The first token refresh under sharing mode irreversibly replaces stored refresh tokens with the placeholder for providers whose refresh path goes through parse (office365, zoom, webex, lark, zoho). If the sync endpoint is ever unreachable, the feature is disabled, or the deployment falls back to direct refresh, every affected credential is dead and users must re-authenticate — a destructive, one-way write performed automatically on the normal refresh path.
